questions.q: Even though raw_customers already exists in Snowflake and dbt is connected to that database, why does it still need to be declared as a dbt source?
options: dbt doesn't know a table exists until it's explicitly declared as a source
Snowflake deletes tables dbt hasn't declared
A source declaration is required before COPY INTO can run
dbt automatically detects every table and never needs a source declaration
questions.explain: Connecting to a database doesn't make dbt aware of specific tables in it — a source declaration is what tells dbt this particular raw table exists and can be referenced.

questions.q: In this lesson's sources.yml, what do the `database:` and `schema:` keys point at?
options: jaffle_shop_raw and public — the exact database and schema raw_customers was loaded into in Lesson 3
The dbt project's own folder name and version
The Snowflake warehouse and role used to run queries
The staging model's and mart model's names
questions.explain: The sources.yml file points dbt at the real jaffle_shop_raw database and public schema from Lesson 3's CREATE DATABASE/CREATE SCHEMA statements.

questions.q: What are the two arguments passed to source() when referencing raw_customers?
options: The source name ('jaffle_shop') and the table name ('raw_customers')
The database name and the warehouse name
The schema name and the column name
The model name and the test name
questions.explain: source('jaffle_shop', 'raw_customers') takes the source name declared in sources.yml and the table name listed under it — not a hardcoded fully-qualified table name.

questions.q: If raw_customers were later moved to a different schema, what would have to change?
options: Only the schema: line in sources.yml — every model using source() would keep working without edits
Every model file in the project that references the table
Nothing — dbt automatically tracks table locations
The dbt project would need to be deleted and recreated
questions.explain: Because models reference the table through source() rather than a hardcoded name, moving the underlying table only requires updating sources.yml in one place.

questions.q: What real convention does this lesson follow for naming and locating the source YAML file?
options: models/staging/jaffle_shop/src_jaffle_shop.yml — next to the staging model that will reference it
sources/raw_customers.sql, in a top-level sources folder
dbt_project.yml, appended to the existing project config
profiles.yml, alongside the Snowflake connection
questions.explain: The real convention places a source's YAML declaration inside models/staging/<source_name>/, named src_<source_name>.yml, right next to the staging model that will use it.
